Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick reply on our interest form. Hoshino Retail would like a short demo to understand how Redwood's serving/runtime could fit our storefront personalization pipeline. We're based in Tokyo (JST) but have staff in SG and SYD. Our ideal window is morning Tokyo time (09:00–11:30 JST), or late SG afternoon (16:00–18:30 SGT) — we want to avoid after-hours in SYD if possible because those colleagues start their day later.

Two quick asks:
- Can you propose 2x 45-minute windows this week in JST and SGT?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's demo invites will show the same day in Tokyo and not roll to the next business day for SG/SYD attendees (we've been burned by cross-day invites before around midnight).

Cheers,
Rie Tanaka
Head of Digital Ops
Hoshino Retail

Aditya / team — quick timezone clarification from ops side:
- Tokyo = JST (UTC+9) — no DST.
- Singapore = SGT (UTC+8) — no DST.
- Sydney = AEDT (UTC+11) — DST active in Nov.

So if we pick Option A at 09:30 JST, Sydney local becomes 11:30 AEDT on the same date. The main risk Marissa and I have seen is when an organizer creates an event using UTC and some calendar clients display the converted time but with a different date because of midnight boundaries. To avoid any confusion:
- We'll create the Google Calendar invite in JST with explicit local times listed in the description.
- We'll include a timezone grid image (apac-timezone-grid.png) in the invite description so recipients in SG/SYD can immediately see local mapping.

I'll cross-post once the invite is created.

—Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
